purpose: Use prediction-market probabilities as one prospective input when estimating whether and how soon U.S. federal legislation may pass before final congressional passage.
governing_question: Can this signal earn and keep the right to influence capital allocation?
interpretation_rules: A Polymarket price is a market-implied probability for the contract's exact resolution condition and deadline; it is not automatically an expected passage date.
When comparable markets exist for multiple deadlines, preserve each probability and construct a passage-probability term structure rather than selecting one favorable contract.
Any inferred incremental probability or passage hazard must be calculated only after verifying that contract definitions are comparable and the deadline probabilities are logically ordered.
Prediction-market information supplements official legislative text, schedules, votes, amendment risk and procedural status; it cannot replace them.
The probability snapshot used in a research decision must have been observable before the exposure mapping and entry decision were sealed.

approved_public_sources.name: Polymarket Gamma API
approved_public_sources.purpose: Discover markets and retain question, description, outcomes, outcome prices, dates, resolution source, activity, liquidity and volume metadata.

approved_public_sources.name: Polymarket CLOB API
approved_public_sources.purpose: Retain executable bid, ask, midpoint, spread, price history and order-book information instead of relying only on a displayed probability.

approved_public_sources.name: Polymarket price methodology
approved_public_sources.purpose: Interpret displayed prices and distinguish midpoint or last-trade display from executable prices.

required_contract_checks: The resolution condition must match the legislative milestone being modeled: House passage, Senate passage, final congressional passage, presidential signature or another explicitly named event must not be conflated.
The deadline and timezone must be explicit and stored in UTC.
The resolution source and market rules must be archived with the snapshot.
The market must be active and accepting orders at the decision timestamp.
Liquidity, volume, bid, ask, midpoint, last trade and spread must be stored; displayed probability alone is insufficient.
Markets with ambiguous wording, unresolved amendment dependence, excessively wide spreads or insufficient liquidity must be excluded or marked low quality.
Related deadline markets must have sufficiently comparable wording before they are treated as a term structure.
prohibited_uses: Do not treat one deadline probability as a precise expected passage date.
Do not use a market whose resolution milestone differs from the legislative milestone in the trade hypothesis.
Do not infer probability from post-entry prices or from a market created after the research decision.
Do not allow the Polymarket probability to become the sole trade trigger.
Do not use displayed probability without recording executable bid-ask conditions.
Do not authorize real-money trading from this design record.
remaining_freeze_blockers: handling when no suitable Polymarket market exists
